messages:
Maria Chen: FYI customer (Acme Payments) is seeing intermittent signing failures when using their CloudHSM-backed key for JWT signing. Started ~08:15 UTC, ~1–2% of requests failing with 500s. Logs show HSM errors.

Kevin O'Leary: Can you paste the exact error from our side? Do we have correlation IDs or sample request/response?

Maria Chen: Correlation IDs: trace=acme-8912,acme-8916. Customer attached snippets, here's the relevant line from our logs:
```
2024-11-18T08:16:23Z ERROR sign-handler request_id=acme-8912 crypto: Sign failed: CKR_DEVICE_ERROR (slot 2) retry=0
2024-11-18T08:16:23Z WARN  sign-handler fallback_attempt=0 reason="no softkey available"
2024-11-18T08:16:25Z ERROR api request_id=acme-8916 status=500 body="hsm: session timeout waiting for slot"
```

Maria Chen: Customer also reports higher end-to-end latency (200ms -> 1.2s p95) around the same time window.

Support Bot: Case created: #SUP-2024-2379 - assigned to Kevin O'Leary. :ticket:

Kevin O'Leary: Thanks. Quick checklist: (1) Are they using CloudHSM in single-AZ or multi-AZ? (2) Which crypto-agent/driver version? (3) Is the key a customer-managed HSM key or a Redwood-provisioned KMS key with HSM backing?

Maria Chen: Answers from customer:
- CloudHSM in us-east-1, single-AZ (they said)
- crypto-agent v1.6.2
- Key is customer-managed in their CloudHSM cluster (we do not store key material)

Kevin O'Leary: Ok. Likely causes: session pool exhaustion, network jitter between Redwood nodes and CloudHSM, or CloudHSM maintenance/firmware issue. Can you ask customer to run a quick repro that exercises signing at higher qps so we can reproduce? Provide this script: 
```
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  start=$(date +%s%3N)
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDFWOOD_KEY" \ 
    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sign?key_id=projects/acme/keys/pm-123" || echo "curl fail"
  end=$(date +%s%3N)
  sleep 0.05
done
```

Kevin O'Leary: Also ask for HSM-side logs (CloudHSM syslog) around the timestamps.

Jenna Patel: tagging Eng Security — any chance this is a key-custody / key-rotation issue? Customer asked whether Redwood ever got vault access; they are worried about extraction during failover.

Eng Security: short answer: Redwood never has plaintext key material for customer-managed CloudHSM keys. We communicate the custody model in the onboarding doc. The current issue looks operational (timeouts) not exfiltration. If customer wants, we can provide an audit log export showing HSM sessions and operator actions for the time window. Which retention window do they need?

Maria Chen: Customer asked for retention last 90 days and a filtered audit of admin ops + HSM session creation. Also wants confirmation that our failover does not migrate keys to a soft HSM in clear.

Eng Security: We can export CloudHSM admin events and Redwood proxy session logs. For the failover model: we do not export or persist plaintext key material. In extreme emergency we have a "soft-sign fallback" mode but it's disabled by default for customer-managed keys and requires explicit opt-in and a signed waiver. We should offer that only as a temporary mitigation with customer approval.

CloudOps: Checking infra: there was a CloudHSM maintenance window in us-east-1 on 2024-11-18 07:50–08:10 UTC (AWS advisory). Coordination notes show a few clusters reported high CPU/IO during patching. I'll attach the maintenance id: aws-hsm-2024-11-18-ue1.

Kevin O'Leary: That aligns with the customer's 08:15 start. Likely transient device-level disruption. Action plan I propose:
1) Ask customer to run the repro script and upload curl outputs.
2) Request CloudHSM syslog + audit for the range 07:30–09:00 UTC.
3) Check our proxy (crypto-agent v1.6.2) session pool metrics and increase pool size on their Dedicated route as a short-term config if they need higher QPS.
4) Offer audit export and formal statement on key custody + explain soft-sign fallback policy (requires waiver).

Maria Chen: Customer willing to run script now. I'll collect outputs and syslog. They've also asked whether we can temporarily route to a different AZ/region for lower latency.

CloudOps: We can route to us-east-2 if customer approves cross-region. Need to verify key replication if any; since this is customer-managed CloudHSM, we can't replicate keys for them. They'd need to provision a cluster in us-east-2 and import the key there. We can help with runbook.

Jenna Patel: Customer also asked about billing — they saw a spike in API errors and were worried about being billed for failed attempts. Support: we should credit failed API calls if caused by our infra incident.

Kevin O'Leary: Agreed. I'll mark for billing review and propose a one-time credit for error-rate window 08:15–08:45 UTC if logs confirm HSM errors were the root cause.

Maria Chen: Uploads from customer: `curl_outputs.txt` (many 500 entries with timing ~1.1–1.4s) and `cloudhsm_syslog.txt` showing repeated `CKR_DEVICE_ERROR` and `session limit reached`. I'll attach to the case.

Support Bot: Note: billing team pinged. Internal thread #BILL-998 created.

Eng Security: I'll prepare a redact-safe audit export (admin events + session creation timestamps). We'll exclude any sensitive key identifiers but include session IDs, source IPs, and operator principals. ETA 3 hours.

Kevin O'Leary: Next steps assigned: Maria to coordinate with customer and collect artifacts; CloudOps to validate maintenance impact; Eng Security to prepare audit export; Billing to evaluate credit. I'll follow up in 4 hours or when artifacts arrive.

Maria Chen: Customer confirmed they want the temporary throughput increase and will provision a second CloudHSM cluster in us-east-2 (they'll handle key import). They're ok with audit export. Thanks team — I'll update case when uploads complete. :white_check_mark:

Jenna Patel: Small note for docs/FAQ: add a short section on "CloudHSM maintenance impact" and our soft-sign fallback policy so CS can reference proactively.

Kevin O'Leary: Good call. I'll draft a short blurb after this is closed.

Maria Chen: Closing loop for now — last update from customer at 09:02 UTC said errors decreased after AWS maintenance completed. Will reopen if they see further regressions.

Support Bot: Case #SUP-2024-2379 status=waiting_on_customer last_update=1729001387
